chapter_note: This chapter is almost entirely oldest teaching substrate. The only editorial element is the dialogue frame formula in ¶1. The teaching describes the First Man's descent, the construction of the universe from captured dark powers, and the devastation of the dark storehouses — using two correspondential analogies (marsh/net and body/head-limbs). The body-cosmos mapping in ¶5-6 is a recognized substrate marker. No institutional, exhortation, or editorial bridge vocabulary appears anywhere in the chapter. Despite heavy lacunae damage throughout, the cosmological process narrative is coherent and systematic.

paragraphs.core_text: At the time when the First Man was sent to the war in the first garment of [living fire], which he gave to the first nature that exists [...] in that single garment. [...] he hunted Matter, the thought of death, [...] and all its other powers.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed opening dialogue frame formula: 'Once again the enlightener speaks:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula is standard Kephalaia compilation marker. The teaching content — First Man's descent in the garment of living fire, hunting Matter — is cosmological process narrative. 'Matter, the thought of death' is a substrate epithet describing the personified cosmic antagonist.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.130⟩ When the First Man came up from the abyss, [...] the Living Spirit brought the rulers whom he had hunted [...] element, that [...] of [the land of] darkness, that he might construct from them this universe and fashion everything appropriate for the greatness. From that time on, the place of the storehouses of the elements [...] he destroyed and laid waste the [...] all that were in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmological process: First Man's ascent, Living Spirit's demiurgic construction from captured rulers, devastation of storehouses. 'Construct from them this universe' and 'fashion everything appropriate for the greatness' describe the cosmic architecture's formation. Heavy lacunae but the process structure is clear.

paragraphs.core_text: Just like a marsh, of which the fish and birds are snared in a net, and only the waters are left behind and the reeds and the plants that grow in it, this is also the case with the storehouses of death. The [First] Man snared their counsels and [their k]in that were [in them], and the storehouses were left behind in their [dwelli]ng place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential analogy mapping natural domain (marsh, fish, birds, net, reeds) onto cosmic domain (storehouses of death, counsels, kin). Both sides of the mapping remain within the cosmic system. The marsh IS the correspondence for the depleted dark storehouses. Classic substrate technique — expounding through natural correspondence.

paragraphs.core_text: So then, the case of the land of darkness is like this, as is that of the storehouses that were in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief transitional summary linking the land of Darkness to its storehouses. Functions as a structural connector between the marsh analogy and the body-head analogy that follows.

paragraphs.core_text: Just as the body of man has many limbs in it, [the land of darkness] has [storehouses from] its beginning [...] all [the limbs] that hang from the great head of the [body]. A single root is the root of them all, because they all hang from the great head that is on top of the body. Should a limb be cut from the tip of [the]se small [h]eads, the great head that is on top of them [al]l stays in its place the way that it is [...] you find this person alive. Al[l] these sm[all h]eads are firmly set in it [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Body-cosmos correspondence: the body's head-limb hierarchy mapped onto the land of Darkness and its storehouses. This is a recognized substrate marker (body-cosmos mapping, cf. Ch. 70). 'A single root is the root of them all' — systematic hierarchical description. Despite lacunae, the structural logic (great head vs. small heads, cutting limbs vs. cutting the head) is the teaching itself.

paragraphs.core_text: Wh[en] they will cut from them [...] all of them, these little [heads] shall [...] the corpses, because they might see [...] be firmly set [...] in the body, which they joined wi[th it ...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the body-head analogy. Very fragmentary — heavy lacunae obscure the exact argument, but the vocabulary (corpses, little heads, body, firmly set) remains within the body-cosmos correspondence domain. No editorial markers despite the damage.

paragraphs.core_text: In exactly this way, it is also the case that the storehouses of darkness are the same, the things from which the [darkness gushed] forth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closing summary applying the body-head analogy back to the storehouses of Darkness. 'The things from which the [darkness gushed] forth' — cosmological process language describing the storehouses' original function. The chapter closes cleanly within the cosmic system with no editorial extension, exhortation, or institutional application.
